key: And he wrote in the letter, saying: ‘Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.’
s: David, having lain with Uriah’s wife, who has conceived, has Uriah killed; Rashi, on 11:15, reads the death as meant to divorce her retroactively under each soldier’s conditional writ, so David had not lain with a married woman, and Metzudat David, on 11:15, as meant to let David marry her, the child seeming conceived in marriage.
src: Rashi and Metzudat David, on 2 Samuel 11:15, Hebrew (Rashi: Sefaria’s “On Your Way”; Metzudat David: “On Your Way”), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

evidence.words: ונכה ומת. כדי שתהא מגורשת למפרע, ונמצא שלא בא על אשת איש, שכל היוצא למלחמה, כותב גט לאשתו על תנאי, אם ימות במלחמה … ושבתם מאחריו. לבל יעזרוהו, ויהיה נכה מבני עמון וימות, וכוונתו היתה לישאנה אחרי זה, למען יחשבו שהרתה אחר הנשואין
evidence.gloss: [Rashi, on 11:15, ‘that he may be smitten, and die’:] So that she would be divorced retroactively, and it would turn out that he had not come upon a married woman, for everyone who goes out to war writes his wife a bill of divorce on condition, if he should die in the war. … [Metzudat David, on 11:15, ‘and retire ye from him’:] So that they would not help him, and he would be struck by the Ammonites and die; and his intention was to marry her after this, so that people would think she had conceived after the marriage.
